findings.documented: Every request must carry the API key appended as a query parameter (?api_key=IVY26-XXXXXXXXXXXX).
findings.actual: Passing the key as a query parameter results in 401 Unauthorized ('send your key in the X-API-Key request header, not as a query parameter'). The API strictly requires the key in the X-API-Key HTTP header.
findings.how_found: Called GET /v1/listings?api_key=... and observed 401 response with instruction to use X-API-Key header.
findings.impact: All API calls fail with 401 Unauthorized if using the documented query parameter authentication.

findings.documented: Returns token, token_type Bearer, expires_in 86400 (24 hours), and user with email and name. Claims single login is enough and there is no refresh flow.
findings.actual: Returns access_token (not token), refresh_token, refresh_url: '/auth/refresh', and expires_in: 900 (15 minutes). User object contains only email, no name. The session expires in 15 minutes, requiring refresh token rotation.
findings.how_found: Called POST /auth/login with valid demo credentials and inspected JSON response fields and values.
findings.impact: Frontend authentication breaks: tokens expire after 15 minutes instead of 24 hours, causing unauthorized errors after 15 minutes without active token refresh.

findings.documented: Explicitly claimed: 'There is no refresh flow.'
findings.actual: POST /auth/refresh exists, accepting {'refresh_token': '...'} and issuing a fresh 15-minute access_token.
findings.how_found: Tested the refresh_url path returned by POST /auth/login with the received refresh_token.
findings.impact: Crucial endpoint for sustaining user sessions beyond 15 minutes without forcing the user to log in again.

findings.documented: Takes page (1-indexed, default 1) and limit (default 20, max 200). Response contains total, page, page_size, results.
findings.actual: The page parameter is quietly ignored. Pagination is zero-indexed using offset and limit. Maximum limit is capped at 50 (passing 100 or 200 still returns 50 records). Response shape is {limit, offset, count, total, has_more, results}.
findings.how_found: Tested varying limit and page parameters; verified page=2 returns identical items to page=1 (offset 0), while offset=50 fetches the next page.
findings.impact: Applications relying on page=2 for pagination stay stuck on the first 20 records. Requests expecting up to 200 items receive only 50.

findings.documented: Claims 'total' is the exact number of records matching filters, and reading 'total' / limit gives the exact number of pages to reach every record.
findings.actual: Server reports total: 4128, but paginating until has_more is false yields 4,400 retrievable listing records (understated by 272 records). Similarly, rentals reports total 1548 but yields 1650; projects reports 441 but yields 470.
findings.how_found: Iterated through offsets past the reported total until has_more was false and count returned 0.
findings.impact: Clients that stop requesting pages when offset reaches the reported 'total' will silently miss 272 listings, 102 rentals, and 29 projects.

findings.documented: Returns active sale listings only. Inactive, expired and withdrawn listings are claimed to be excluded server side.
findings.actual: Returns both active and inactive listings. Each listing object carries an 'is_live' boolean field. Exactly 923 out of 4,400 retrievable listings have is_live: false.
findings.how_found: Inspected listing records and observed is_live boolean property with both true and false values.
findings.impact: Frontends displaying all listings without checking is_live will show unavailable and withdrawn properties to users.

findings.actual: GET /v1/listing/{listing_id} returns 404 Not Found. The actual working endpoint is plural: GET /v1/listings/{listing_id}.
findings.how_found: Invoked GET /v1/listing/MAG-2001953 (got 404), then tried plural /v1/listings/MAG-2001953 (got 200 OK).
findings.impact: Individual property detail pages fail to load if using the documented singular path.

findings.documented: GET /v1/listings/{listing_id}/similar returns up to ten comparable listings.
findings.actual: Returns 404 Not Found for valid listing IDs.
findings.how_found: Sent GET request to /v1/listings/MAG-2001953/similar and received 404.
findings.impact: Similar listings carousel cannot be fetched directly from the server; client must compute recommendations.

findings.documented: GET /v1/favourites, POST /v1/favourites with body {'id': '...'}, and DELETE /v1/favourites/{id}.
findings.actual: All /v1/favourites routes return 404 Not Found. The active endpoint is /v1/saved, and the POST payload strictly requires {'listing_id': '...'} rather than {'id': '...'}.
findings.how_found: Probed /v1/favourites (404), probed /v1/saved (200 OK), sent {'id': '...'} and observed 422 error requiring 'listing_id'.
findings.impact: Saved listings/favourites feature fails completely if using the documented routes and payloads.

findings.documented: Not in documentation; documentation specifies /v1/favourites instead.
findings.actual: GET /v1/saved lists saved properties, POST /v1/saved with {'listing_id': '...'} adds a saved listing, and DELETE /v1/saved/{listing_id} removes it.
findings.how_found: Scanned alternative route naming patterns and validated CRUD operations.
findings.impact: Required endpoint for implementing user bookmarking.

findings.documented: GET /v1/analytics/summary returns pre-computed city statistics (median_price, by_locality, by_bhk).
findings.how_found: Tested GET /v1/analytics/summary with valid auth headers and received 404 Not Found.
findings.impact: Insights screen cannot rely on precomputed server aggregates and must aggregate metrics directly from listings data.

findings.documented: Claims price_min and price_max are integers in Indian rupees (e.g. 8900000, 21400000).
findings.actual: price_min and price_max are floating point values denominated in Lakhs (when >= 10, e.g. 37.9 Lakhs) and Crores (when < 10, e.g. 1.21 Crores), not in raw rupees.
findings.how_found: Compared project price ranges with actual listing prices within each project (e.g. P20001 has price_min 65.2 and price_max 1.21 against listings priced 6.35M to 25.49M INR).
findings.impact: Displaying project prices without unit conversion shows prices of 1 to 99 rupees instead of Lakhs and Crores.

findings.documented: min_price, max_price, and furnishing query parameters filter listings server side.
findings.actual: min_price, max_price, and furnishing query parameters are accepted but quietly ignored. The server returns the unfiltered total (4,128) and unmatching records.
findings.how_found: Queried /v1/listings with min_price=10000000&max_price=12000000 and furnishing=unfurnished; responses included out-of-range prices and fully-furnished listings with total count unchanged.
findings.impact: Clients relying solely on server filtering will present wrong search results to users unless client-side filtering is applied.

findings.documented: total_listings always agrees with what GET /v1/listings?project_id=... returns.
findings.actual: The project_id parameter on GET /v1/listings is quietly ignored, returning all listings in the city rather than filtering by project.
findings.how_found: Queried GET /v1/listings?project_id=P20001 and received all 4,128 city listings.
findings.impact: Project detail pages cannot load project-specific listings using the query parameter without client filtering.

findings.documented: total_listings always agrees with the number of listings currently available in the project.
findings.actual: For 129 out of 470 projects, total_listings does not match the count of active listings for that project in /v1/listings.
findings.how_found: Counted active listings per project_id across all listings and compared against project.total_listings.
findings.impact: Project cards and details show out-of-sync available unit counts.

findings.documented: Claims each listing corresponds to exactly one physical property.
findings.actual: Multiple listing records describe the exact same physical property (identical apartment, floor, total floors, bedrooms, carpet area, facing direction) across different listing websites and brokers.
findings.how_found: Grouped listings by composite physical property attributes; found 20 duplicate listings across 4,380 distinct properties.
findings.impact: Users see identical apartments listed multiple times at slightly varying prices by different brokers.

findings.documented: Listings describe genuine, safe-to-show real estate properties.
findings.actual: 50 listing records contain physically impossible data: 10 with negative prices, 10 with floor > total_floors, 10 with carpet area > super built up area, 10 with latitude > 50 placing them in the Arctic Ocean, and 10 non-plot properties with 0 bedrooms.
findings.how_found: Ran automated domain constraint audits over all numerical and geographical fields.
findings.impact: Causes UI display bugs, broken coordinate maps, and distorted price-per-square-foot metrics.

findings.documented: All listings are genuine sale offerings.
findings.actual: Contains fake/fraudulent listings designed to generate leads or advance-fee scams. 72 listings demand advance token payments ('Pay a token amount of Rs 25,000 today') or booking fees before site visits, posted by 7 telephone numbers using rotating fictitious agency names. 10 listings feature bait prices under Rs 16,000 for entire villas and apartments.
findings.how_found: Conducted NLP text analysis on listing descriptions and clustered contact numbers with multiple agency names.
findings.impact: Exposes users to advance-fee deposit scams and deceptive lead generation.
